title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 225 (Compensation to agent for injury caused by principal’s neglect)

content.overview: Section 225 provides that the principal must make compensation to his agent in respect of injury caused to such agent by the principal’s neglect or want of skill. Illustration: A employs B as a bricklayer and puts up the scaffolding himself unskilfully; B is hurt — A must compensate B.
content.glance: Principal must compensate agent for injury caused by principal’s neglect or want of skill.
content.study: The principal must compensate the agent for injury caused by the principal’s neglect or want of skill. Illustration: A employs B as a bricklayer in building a house and puts up the scaffolding himself; the scaffolding is unskilfully put up and B is hurt; A must make compensation to B. Current-law framing: identify the injury; link it to the principal’s neglect or want of skill; conclude on the duty to compensate.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 225 apply to injury caused by a third party unrelated to the principal’s neglect?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 225 is limited to injury caused by the principal’s neglect or want of skill.

misconceptions.trap: The principal never compensates the agent for workplace injury.
misconceptions.correction: Section 225 requires compensation where injury is caused by the principal’s neglect or want of skill.
